articles.title: Exercise Beverly Sunrise 27-01
articles.summary: U.S. Airmen assigned to the 35th Fighter Wing, alongside joint mission partners, participated in Exercise Beverly Sunrise 27-01 at Misawa Air Base, Japan, Oct. 19-23. The exercise tested their ability to respond to simulated threats, sustain operations and project combat power in contested environments.

articles.title: U.S., Republic of Korea navies successfully conclude Maritime Counter-Special Operations Exercise
articles.summary: Naval forces from the U.S. and Republic of Korea (ROK) successfully concluded the bilateral Maritime Counter-Special Operations Forces Exercise (MCSOFEX) in the waters surrounding the Pyeongtaek, Republic of Korea, Oct 23, 2026.

articles.title: La. Guard begins construction on Lake Charles Field Maintenance Shop

articles.title: Thunderbirds arrive in Wichita ahead of Frontiers in Flight Air Show
articles.summary: MCCONNELL AIR FORCE BASE, Kan. — The roar of fighter jets is set to fill the skies over the Air Capital of the World as the U.S. Air Force Thunderbirds arrive at McConnell Air Force Base, Kansas, ahead of the 2026 Frontiers in Flight Air Show and Open House Oct. 24-25.

articles.title: OLDCC funding supports water system resiliency planning for West Kauai and PMRF
articles.summary: KEKAHA, HAWAII – The Department of Water, County of Kauai (KDOW), in partnership with the U.S. Navy’s Pacific Missile Range Facility (PMRF), is advancing critical water-infrastructure planning for the Kekaha-Waimea water system through support from the Office of Local Defense Community Cooperation (OLDCC).

Scott Berkheimer, a pediatrician at Naval Hospital Twentynine Palms, was named Navy Pediatrician of the Year by the American Academy of Pediatrics Section on Uniformed Services in October 2026, recognizing his professional accomplishments and dedication to caring for military-connected children and families.

articles.title: Blount Island team briefs assistant commandant on sustaining Marines ashore
articles.summary: On the ramp of USNS Dahl, U.S. Marine Corps Sgt. Jeremiah Murray gave his service’s second-highest-ranking officer a firsthand account of how his team equips Marines overseas.

articles.title: From runway to reps: Black Hawk pilot soars to the top of Army fitness
articles.summary: Warrant Officer Sorenson, a member of the highly competitive U.S. Army Warrior Fitness Team and a UH-60M Black Hawk helicopter pilot, aims to inspire others to pursue fitness by demonstrating that determination and hard work can turn even the most ambitious goals into reality.

articles.summary: DILLON, Mont. — The Montana National Guard partnered with the Montana Youth Challenge Academy (MYCA) and the University of Montana Western to bring educators from across the state to Dillon, Oct. 21, for a firsthand look at a program helping young Montanans build brighter futures.

articles.title: The Beast meets the Bats: Iowa Airmen welcome Secret Service
articles.summary: Iowa Air National Guard Airmen assigned to the 185th Air Refueling Wing welcomed U.S. Secret Service personnel prior to a presidential visit to Sioux City, Iowa, Oct. 22, 2026.

articles.summary: FORT HOOD, Texas — U.S. Army Garrison-Fort Hood held a change of responsibility Friday at III Armored Corps Headquarters, passing responsibility from Command Sgt. Maj. Loyd Rhoades to Command Sgt. Maj. Kristopher Tate.

articles.title: Historic Accord: Naval Weapons Station Yorktown and Federally Recognized Native American Tribes Sign Landmark NAGPRA Agreement

The agreement is the first of its kind within any U.S. Navy installation within the Commander, Navy Region Mid-Atlantic Area of Responsibility.

articles.title: ASC awards top ammo inspectors for munitions safety
articles.summary: Three employees from U.S. Army Sustainment Command have been recognized as Quality Assurance Specialist (Ammunition Surveillance) of the Year for their role in munitions safety and quality.

articles.title: U.S. Air Force Band kicks off Montana fall tour
articles.summary: The U.S. Air Force Concert Band and Singing Sergeants launched their autumn tour with a performance at the Alberta Bair Theater in Billings, Montana, Oct. 14.

articles.title: Cleveland Harbor Fall Dredging Starting; Supports Safe Great Lakes Navigation, Strengthens Local and National Economy
articles.summary: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Buffalo District, will begin fall dredging this week in Cleveland Harbor to maintain safe and navigable waterways for Great Lakes commercial vessels, recreational boaters and other harbor users on Lake Erie. The Buffalo District awarded an $11.7 million contract in April 2026 to New York-based DMYLES, Inc.

articles.title: ‘Ability to strike back’: Denmark commits to long-range missile orders

articles.title: South Dakota Guard's 155th Engineer Company honored before southern border deployment
articles.summary: More than 120 Soldiers of the South Dakota Army National Guard's 155th Engineer Company were honored at an activation ceremony Oct. 22 at Wagner Community School. The Soldiers are deploying to the southern border in support of Operation Ardent Vanguard. The Wagner-based unit will deploy under the direction of U.S. Northern Command.

articles.title: The Pentagon has gone too far in using the Other Transaction Authority. Congress should act.
articles.summary: Created in 1958 for NASA, the obscure fiscal tool has since become the predominant approach to military contracting – at great risk to taxpayers, one researcher warns.

articles.summary: Soon, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New York District will be cleaning up the Middlesex Municipal Landfill FUSRAP site in Middlesex, New Jersey and applying an innovative soil sorting system that will save tax-payer money, reduce air pollution, and most importantly return the land back to the community.
